title: Amazing NAN Marathon 2026 Review: What the Race Was Like
seo_title: Amazing NAN Marathon Review: Start Times, Cut-offs, Results
meta_description: Amazing NAN Marathon 2026 review: a 3am marathon start from Wat Phumin, saturated 24°C air at dawn, a 6:30 cut-off, courses that measured long and how fast 3,200 finishers ran.
dek: What northern Thailand's old-town marathon was like on 1 November 2026: the early starts, the dawn air, the cut-offs, the distances the timing system actually measured, and how fast the field ran.
verdict: Enter if you want a relaxed, mid-sized marathon in one of Thailand's best-preserved old towns, with a generous field of slower runners. The 2026 race started and finished beside Wat Phumin, and its marathon left at 3am so most of it was run in the dark. Dawn air at Nan airport was 24°C and fully saturated, with no wind, warming to 28°C by 9am. Two things to know: the 6:30 marathon cut-off is tighter than many Thai races, and the timed courses measured long, at 42.4 km and 21.2 km.

sections.heading: The Course: An Old-Town Start, Measured Long
paragraphs: All four races start and finish at Khuang Mueang Nan, the square beside Wat Phumin that hosts Nan's night food market [8]. The Tourism Authority of Thailand listed it as a run through the historic streets and cultural landmarks of Nan [9]. No course map or written route was published on the entry page, so runners met the route on the day.

The timing system's own checkpoints show the courses ran long: the finish lines were set at 42.4 km for the marathon, 21.2 km for the half, 10.5 km for the 10 km and 5.11 km for the 5 km [11]. Allow for an extra 200 m in a marathon pace plan. Timing mats sat at 10 km and 37.2 km on the marathon, and at 10 km and 17 km on the half [11].

sections.heading: The Weather: Saturated and Still Before Dawn
paragraphs: Nan airport, about 4 km north of the start, does not report overnight, so there is no observation for the 3am marathon start. From 5am, when the half marathon left, to 7am it recorded 24°C with a dew point of 24°C, 100% humidity, wind of 1 to 3 knots and only a few clouds [10]. It then warmed quickly: 27°C at 8am, 28°C at 9am and 30°C at 10am [10].

Air that is completely saturated stops sweat from evaporating, even at 24°C. A five-hour marathoner finished at 8am at 27°C in sunshine, and anyone near the 9.30am cut-off was running in 28°C to 30°C. On this morning the humidity, not the temperature, set the pace.

sections.heading: Cut-offs, Aid and Rules
paragraphs: The cut-offs were 6 hours 30 for the marathon, 4 hours for the half, 2 hours for the 10 km and 1 hour for the 5 km, and runners outside them were to be recorded as DNF [1][2]. Seven marathon finishers (2.4%) are listed with times beyond 6:30, while every half marathoner finished inside four hours [11].

The organiser did not publish the number or spacing of drinks stations. The rules allow help only at official service points, ban private pacers and disqualify littering on the course [1]. Every entry included accident insurance and chip timing [3].

sections.heading: How Fast the Field Is
paragraphs: This is a recreational race with a quick front. The marathon was won in 2:59:51 by a man and 3:48:56 by a woman, and tenth place overall was 3:34:26 [11]. Behind them, 289 marathoners finished with a median of 5:22:04; the slowest tenth took more than 6:25, only 12% broke four hours and 40% broke five, and 22% of finishers were women [11].

The half marathon had 885 finishers. It was won in 1:28:04 and 1:46:57, tenth place was 1:35:56, the median was 2:29:19, 18% broke two hours, and 31% of finishers were women [11]. The 10 km was the biggest race, with 1,331 finishers, a median of 1:18:06, 17% under an hour and almost half of them women [11].

About 4,385 entrants were listed across the four races, but roughly a quarter did not start: 70 of 377 in the marathon and 323 of 1,223 in the half [11]. Trophies go to the top three overall and the top five in each age group, with no prize money [6].

sections.heading: Race Weekend Logistics
paragraphs: Bibs were collected only on Saturday 31 October, noon to 6pm, at the start area, with no collection on race morning; runners needed their bib number and an ID card or passport [1][7]. Left luggage opened at 2am on race day [2].

Every entry came with a race shirt and finisher medal, and marathon and half finishers inside the cut-off got a finisher shirt [3]. For a higher fee, runners could buy a SUB shirt earned by going under four hours in the marathon, two hours in the half or an hour in the 10 km [4]; on the 2026 results, 34 marathoners, 158 half marathoners and 227 10 km runners made those marks [11]. Fees rose from THB 999 to 1,200 for the marathon and THB 800 to 900 for the half across three price tiers [5].

sections.heading: Should You Enter the Next Race?
paragraphs: Yes, if you want a friendly, mid-sized race in a beautiful small city, and you are comfortable with a 3am start and a night run. The half marathon, starting at 5am with a four-hour limit, is the easiest entry point: everyone who finished it in 2026 made the cut.
Think twice if your marathon finish is close to 6:30: the limit is tight for a course that measured 42.4 km, and half the field took more than 5:22.
A 2027 date had not been announced when this was written.
Nobody from this site ran the race. This review draws on the organiser's entry page and race graphics, the full results, and airport weather records.

faqs.question: What time does the Amazing NAN Marathon start?
faqs.answer: In 2026 the marathon started at 3am from Khuang Mueang Nan beside Wat Phumin, the half marathon at 5am, the 10 km at 5.30am and the 5 km at 5.45am. Left luggage opened at 2am. Bibs had to be collected the day before, as none were handed out on race morning.

faqs.question: What is the cut-off at the Amazing NAN Marathon?
faqs.answer: In 2026 the limits were 6 hours 30 for the marathon, 4 hours for the half marathon, 2 hours for the 10 km and 1 hour for the 5 km. Every half-marathon finisher made the limit, while seven marathon finishers were listed beyond 6:30 on a course the timing system measured at 42.4 km.

faqs.question: How hot is the Amazing NAN Marathon?
faqs.answer: Humid rather than hot at the start. Nan airport recorded 24°C with 100% humidity and almost no wind from 5am to 7am on race morning in 2026. It reached 27°C by 8am and 28°C by 9am, so marathoners finishing after five hours ran their last kilometres in sunshine.

faqs.question: How many runners finish the Amazing NAN Marathon?
faqs.answer: In 2026, 289 runners finished the marathon, 885 the half marathon, 1,331 the 10 km and 727 the 5 km, out of about 4,385 entrants. Half the marathon finishers took longer than 5:22 and only 12% broke four hours, so slower runners have plenty of company.

editorial_notes: Written 2026-11-06 about the edition that ran on Sunday 1 November 2026, five days earlier; the next edition's date was not found. Finish-time figures are Run SEA's analysis of the official RunResults (Sportman) results; counts of entrants, non-starters and course lengths are from the same results system's category data. Weather is from Nan Nakhon Airport METAR, about 4 km north of the start; the airport has no reports before 5am, so the 3am start is not covered. No course map, aid-station plan or post-race report was found; the organiser's Facebook page could not be read. Aggregators describe the race as hosted by the Tourism Authority of Thailand; the entry page names Route Map Co., Ltd. as organiser. SUB-shirt counts are finishers under the thresholds on the results, not shirt sales. No rating.
